Mapping out the most ambitious
businesses in Scotland in 2020

What we mean by ‘ambitious’
We use 8 criteria to identify high-growth and ambitious 
companies. Each of these is a sign of external validation 
that a business is either actively growing or creating 
ambitious growth plans. 
All companies featured in this report have met at least one 
of these growth triggers.
Equity investment
Accelerator attendance
Scaleups
MBO/MBI
Venture debt
Grant recipients
High-growth lists
Academic spinouts

There are 2,137 active, ambitious companies in Scotland. 
This marks an increase of 195 newly tracked companies in 
the last 12 months, and represents 8% of all ambitious 
companies in the UK. 
A further 707 companies have previously hit one of our 
tracking triggers, but are now no longer trading. 146 of these 
companies have died within the last 12 months. This is a 
higher death rate than in other areas of the country, where 
just 16% of ambitious businesses have died.  
176 have successfully exited the private market, either 
through an IPO or an acquisition. 43 of these exit events 
have taken place in the last 12 months.
Stages of Evolution
Stages of evolution of ambitious businesses in Scotland

Attending a competitive accelerator programme is the most 
popular method of growth for ambitious companies in 
Scotland. This diﬀers from England and Wales, where equity 
fundraising is the most common method of growth. 
Scotland also has an unusually high proportion of spinout 
companies. 6% of ambitious businesses have been spun out 
from an academic institution — double the UK average. 
Methods of Growth
The prevalence of companies growing through 
accelerators is due in no small part to Natwest’s 
Entrepreneur Accelerator (operating as RBS in Scotland). 
Given the sophistication of the country’s angel networks 
and the support of the Scottish Investment Bank, it’s not 
surprising that the proportion of equity-backed 
businesses matches the south of England.
Most popular methods of growth in Scotland
HENRY WHORWOOD, HEAD OF RESEARCH & CONSULTANCY

Most of the ambitious companies in Scotland operate 
business and professional services or in the industrials 
sector. Technology is the third most common sector. 
Within tech, artificial intelligence is the most common 
buzzword, with 47 companies operating in the space. 
The majority of these are based in Edinburgh, making it 
the third top AI-cluster in the UK, behind London and 
Cambridge.
Fintech, edtech and digital security are also popular 
areas of operation. 
Sectors
Top tech sectors in Scotland by number of companies

The coronavirus outbreak has had a massive impact on 
businesses across the UK. But those in Scotland have been 
slightly harder hit. 
This impact has diminished over time, with several hundred 
companies moving from a negative to low impact over the 
past few months. As it stands, 39% of ambitious businesses 
in Scotland are experiencing a low impact from the 
pandemic, and 14% are thought to be seeing a positive 
impact. This includes a surge in demand and creating job 
opportunities. 3% of businesses are in the critical category. 
Across the rest of the UK, the numbers are slightly more 
positive. 45% of businesses are currently experiencing a low 
impact, 18% a positive impact, and just 1% are in the critical 
category.

2017 was an  especially active year for equity investments 
in Scotland. 213 deals were completed, with a combined 
worth of £552m. 2019 was another strong year, with a 
record 214 deals completed. But this activity looks set to 
drop in 2020, and by quite a long way at that. 
Just 73 investments have been announced in the first half 
of this year, totalling £77.5m. If investor activity continues 
on this same trajectory through the second half of the year, 
then 2020 could see the smallest amount of investment for 
Scottish businesses since 2013.

access finance in the wake of lockdown. If they were 
raising in line with the rest of the UK, we would expect 
nearly £150m to have been raised so far this year. 
HENRY WHORWOOD, HEAD OF RESEARCH & CONSULTANCY

14% of all accelerated businesses in the UK reside in 
Scotland. The most popular programme is Entrepreneurial 
Spark, which has accelerated 880 Scottish businesses.
The Entrepreneurial Spark programme originally ran in 
partnership with the Royal Bank of Scotland’s Entrepreneur 
Accelerator network. In 2018, after three years, the bank 
brought the fully funded programme in-house, and has so 
far supported 353 companies in Scotland. Two-thirds of 
these have been accelerated in the past 12 months. 
Accelerator programmes are also the most common method 
of growth for women-owned businesses, with female 
founders often opting for structured programmes instead of 
more transactional funding like equity investment. This may 
explain why Scotland is a popular place for female-founders 
to grow their businesses. 
Accelerators
Top accelerator programmes by number of Scottish companies 
attended since 2011

Scotland has one of the highest rates of ambitious 
female-founded businesses in the UK. Currently, 31% of 
ambitious businesses have at least one female founder, 
second only to Northern Ireland, where 33% of ambitious 
businesses have a female founder. 
But it’s not all good news for women entrepreneurs in 
Scotland. Those companies that have all-female founding 
teams have an incredibly high death rate at 33%, and an exit 
rate of just 1%. These figures stand at 24% and 2% across 
the rest of the UK. 
Meanwhile, mixed gender teams have the lowest death rate 
at 13%, and an exit rate of 3%. 
All-male founding teams have the highest exit rate at 5%, 
and a death rate of 19%. 
Female founders
Exit and death rates in Scotland by gender of founding team

Scotland is already home to a strong aerospace technology and 
manufacturing industry, with 16 ambitious companies operating 
in the area. 
These companies have now been given an extra boost, as local 
authorities have approved plans to launch rockets from the 
Highlands. 
This means small commercial satellites and launch vehicles 
designed and manufactured in Scotland could be taking oﬀ from 
Sutherland within the next few years, with up to 12 launched each 
year. 
Additional Spaceports are planned in other parts of the country, 
including Shetland. Plus, an aerospace centre of excellence will 
be built adjacent to RAF Lossiemouth in the north-east Scotland 
— facilitated by £33m of funding from government and local 
partners.

Top 5 Scottish startups and scaleups
We’ve profiled the five companies that have secured the largest pre-money 
valuations in Scotland. Unsurprisingly, Brewdog tops the list, after attaining a 
valuation of £1.71b in October 2018. But who else has made the ranking?

Around 22% of the privately-held company is owned by 
120,000 beer-drinking investors who bought shares through 
BrewDog’s crowdfunding campaign called “Equity for 
Punks”. The brewery also has backing from investors TSG 
Consumer Partners. 
Recently, the company has been helping in the fight against 
COVID-19 by making hand sanitiser at its distillery in 
Aberdeenshire and donated thousands of units to the NHS. 
1.   Brewdog | £1.71b 
Founded  2006
Sector  Food & Drinks
Location  Aberdeenshire
BrewDog produces its own beer and operates a number of 
bars across the world. Founded back in 2007, by James Watt 
and Martin Dickie in the North East of Scotland, they began 
to brew their own beers after becoming tired of the 
industrially brewed lagers and ales that were dominating 
the UK market. In just 13 years, Brewdog has gone on to 
become one of the UK's fastest-growing brands and an 
industry leader in the craft beer market, having secured a 
staggering £287m in financial backing and an additional 
£2.38m in grants.

raised £32.6m of equity funding to date, across seven funding

Genius secured a pre-money valuation of £102m at a £4.25m

The first Genius loaf hit the shelves in 2009. 12 years later, 
Lucinda is now a Non-Executive Director of the established 
company, which has a global footprint and a wide variety of
